$comment: Known high/critical advisories, accepted deliberately. Each needs a reason. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit-gate.mjs --update`, then write the reasons.

GHSA-28wg-ghj8-5hjv.title: nanoid: non-secure generators can loop indefinitely with negative size
GHSA-28wg-ghj8-5hjv.reason: Transitive, dev-tooling only. The DoS needs a negative or zero size passed to a non-secure generator; no first-party code calls nanoid at all — every id in the product comes from newId() (ULID) or crypto.randomBytes.

GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8.title: nanoid: custom generators can loop indefinitely when size is zero
GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8.reason: Transitive, dev-tooling only. The DoS needs a negative or zero size passed to a non-secure generator; no first-party code calls nanoid at all — every id in the product comes from newId() (ULID) or crypto.randomBytes.

GHSA-37j7-fg3j-429f.title: Happy DOM: VM Context Escape can lead to Remote Code Execution
GHSA-37j7-fg3j-429f.reason: Dev-only (vitest DOM environment); never in the deployed bundle. The VM-escape requires evaluating attacker-controlled HTML, and our tests only ever render our own components. Upgrading 16 to 20 is a major bump across the whole test suite; tracked separately.

GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp.title: brace-expansion: DoS via exponential-time expansion of consecutive non-expanding {} groups
GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp.reason: Transitive through glob/minimatch in build and lint tooling. The DoS needs an attacker-supplied glob pattern; ours are literals in config.

GHSA-4c8g-83qw-93j6.title: fast-uri vulnerable to host confusion via failed IDN canonicalization
GHSA-4c8g-83qw-93j6.reason: Transitive via the JSON-schema/validation toolchain used at build time. The host-confusion variants matter for URL authorization decisions; our only user-supplied-URL path is the tenant-theming fetch, which validates with its own guarded-fetch (DNS-pinned, per-hop revalidated) rather than fast-uri.

GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6.title: Prototype Pollution in sheetJS
GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6.reason: No upstream fix exists — SheetJS left the npm registry, so there is no version to move to. Mitigated instead: the only parse path (XLSX.read in template-import-xlsx.ts) is now gated on templates.create/manage, was already capped at 20 MB, and is rate-limited. The write paths (aoa_to_sheet) do not reach the vulnerable parser.

GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9.title: SheetJS Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)

GHSA-5wm8-gmm8-39j9.title: fast-xml-builder allows attribute values with unwanted quotes to bypass malicious or unwanted attributes
GHSA-5wm8-gmm8-39j9.reason: Transitive via the AWS SDK. Reached only when building XML request bodies to R2 from values we control (object keys, which are regex-validated), not from user input.

GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp.title: When Vitest UI server is listening, arbitrary file can be read and executed
GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp.reason: Dev-only test runner, never deployed. The advisory requires the Vitest UI server to be listening, which we never start (CI runs "vitest run", not "vitest --ui"). Fixing needs vitest 2 to 3, a major bump across 186 test files; tracked separately.

GHSA-7w99-5wm4-3g79.title: @better-auth/oauth-provider's OAuth authorization-code grant allows concurrent redemption when two token requests race t
GHSA-7w99-5wm4-3g79.reason: Not applicable: every remaining better-auth advisory is an OAuth / OIDC-provider / device-authorization / magic-link issue, and this deployment enables none of them (emailAndPassword disabled, email-OTP only, no oidcProvider). The one that did apply — stale sessions after user deletion — is fixed in our own code: isUserActive() revokes on the request path regardless of stored session state. Upgrading to 1.6.29 was attempted and reverted: it pulls better-call@1.4 which requires zod 4, and migrating ~40 routers from zod 3 is not a security patch.
